sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Poitiers is using price and free time, not restriction, to bring people into the centre. A council vote of 30 January 2023 set the on-street rates from 1 March 2023: orange (central) 2.00 euros for one hour, green 1.50 euros and purple 0.40 euro per hour, with the first 30 minutes free if the plate is registered and a post-parking charge of 40 euros, or 25 euros if paid within 96 hours [0]. Resident permits were set at 20 euros a month in the central and residential zones, limited to two per household [1]. We did not check whether these tariffs are still current. Grand Poitiers announced that from Saturday 4 July 2026 the first 1h30 would be free every Saturday from 8:00 to 19:00 in seven covered or enclosed city-centre car parks, with a reduced tariff for motorised two- and three-wheelers [2]; the city magazine also said the free time would apply on street in a sector between the Boivre and the Clain [3]. Before that, a survey in June 2026 asked how people travel and park in the centre on Saturdays; no results were found [5]. From 1 July 2026 the Vitalis bus network was to be free on Saturdays and on Wednesday afternoons [4].

The Mobility Plan 2025-2035 sets the longer frame. Its diagnosis says the city-centre car parks were never saturated in 2019 except briefly at Christmas: average occupancy was 46%, the maximum 86%, reached about 100 hours a year, with 2,993 paid on-street and 3,225 public off-street spaces [7]. The plan proposes a shared-parking strategy starting with four sectors of parking pressure, a study on how Grand Poitiers manages its car parks and a park-and-ride strategy, since there is no structured park-and-ride yet [6][8]. The national register of low-emission zones has no entry for Poitiers, which is an absence in a register and not an official statement [16].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The Notre-Dame Marché car park is the main story. Grand Poitiers closed it in an emergency in June 2024 to guarantee users' safety; a structural study found a lack of strength because of construction defects and water infiltration, 12,000 props were installed and the community intends a complete requalification, which it calls complex [9]. It announced on 13 June 2025 that level -1 would partly reopen on 19 June 2025 with about a hundred spaces, without subscriptions, at 0.40 euro per quarter-hour for the first three hours [10]. The authority's car park list now shows 146 spaces [12]. Meanwhile it added 88 spaces at the Palais de Justice car park for summer 2025 and about 150 cameras at the Hôtel de Ville car park, and offered free shuttles during the closure [11]. Four of its car parks have reserved charging bays, 41 in total [13].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Grand Poitiers runs its own car parks: Toumaï at the station (144 minute-stop and 622 spaces), Théâtre-Auditorium (320), Blossac-Tison (695), Hôtel de Ville (623), Notre-Dame Marché (146), Clos des Carmes (150, subscription only) and Palais de Justice; two private ones are listed, Effia at the station (480) and Q-Park Les Cordeliers (290) [12]. Q-Park itself states 318 spaces and 17 charging points for Les Cordeliers and shows no hourly tariff [14]. Display panels show free spaces on the approach roads, and the page links to an open data set, which we could not open [15]. A local weekly reported in 2017 that entries into the five municipal car parks rose 6.5% in 2016 to over 1.5 million [17].

Our data cover nine car parks with 3,531 spaces from the city's live feed, measured since 5 October 2026. Occupancy averaged about 49% on weekdays and 40% at weekends, weighted by spaces, which is close to the 46% average the Mobility Plan reports for 2019 [7]. The Théâtre car park (320) is the fullest at 70% on weekdays and the station garage Toumaï (640 in the feed) at 66%, and both reached full in single readings. Blossac-Tison (665) is quieter at 38% and Les Cordeliers at 33%. The Palais de Justice car park averages 39% on weekdays but 4% at weekends, while Notre-Dame Marché (146 in the feed) is at 29%. These are two and a half weeks of data, before the Saturday offer could be judged.
